title: Phone-agent spec
description: Everything a generic policy engine needs to run one bank's late-payment calls. Write every value from the brief material and the tool API. A switch the brief does not settle is the string "not_specified": never fill it from habit or from another bank. Templates are what the agent says, word for word; placeholders are {{name}}.

refs.description: Ids of the digest rules this part comes from.

situation_ref.description: The id of an entry in situations[], or not_specified.

expr.description: An expression in the spec expression language (see the prompt).

target.description: A situation id (the call ends there; a transfer when it has a queue), continue (the agent goes back to what it was asking), or not_specified.

retries.description: Further calls with the same values after a failure, before giving up.

on_exhausted.description: Situation when every call failed; its say text tells the customer honestly.

value.description: call_var: a call-variable role. engine: an engine role, or a list of two roles for a joined field. literal: the fixed value. template: a string with {{role}} placeholders.

convert.description: Optional converter, for engine values only.

call_variables.description: Every variable the brief says a call starts with, under its exact name.

bindings.description: How the engine's roles map onto this tool API. The roles, converters and rules are listed in the prompt.

tools.description: Tool role -> tool name. Bind every tool of the API that fits a role.

request.description: Tool role -> {body field path -> field binding}. Every required body field is bound.

response.description: Tool role -> {response role -> response path}; the product list role also has item: {item role -> path inside one item}.

holidays.description: Every non-business date as an explicit date. A holiday given by name becomes its dates for this year and the next two. Empty when the brief names none.

weekday_semantics.description: What a weekday after this or next means. calendar_week: 'this' is that weekday in the current Monday-to-Sunday week and 'next' the one in the following week. nearest: both mean the first such weekday after today. A weekday said alone is always the first one from today on.

named_periods.description: Period words the material gives an exact date to (for example a rule that a named payday or part of a month means a certain business day). Empty when it gives none. A period the material calls vague is not listed here.

phrase.description: The words, lower case, as a customer would say them.

date.description: Expression for the date the words mean.

template.description: The agent's first words, spoken to whoever answers, ending with the question that asks whether the intended person is on the line. Only call-variable placeholders.

required_content.description: Each thing the brief requires in the first words, as a short phrase.

forbidden_before_verification.description: Words the agent must not say to anyone before identity is verified: the brief's words, plus the spoken name of every product kind when the brief forbids naming the product. Lower case.

counts_as_yes.description: Answers that confirm the intended person is speaking, as the brief lists them (a description such as 'their own name' is fine).

max_asks.description: Asks of the confirmation question in total, the first one included.

question_then_reask_counts.description: true when the brief says: if the person asks a question instead, answer it, and the ask after the answer counts as the next ask.

on_unclear.description: Situation when the person is still not confirmed after max_asks.

third_party.description: Someone other than the intended person is on the line.

may_answer_identity.description: Whether a third party may answer the security questions.

ask_reachable_template.description: Asks when the intended person can be reached, without saying why the agent calls.

deflect_template.description: Reply when a third party asks about the call or the account or offers to help; reveals nothing and asks again when the person can be reached.

enabled.description: Whether the agent books a callback for a third party.

day_rule.description: Boolean expression over d (the offered date), today and now: true when a callback on d is allowed.

windows.description: Allowed clock times on an allowed day.

after_now.description: The callback must be later than the current time.

granularity_minutes.description: Callback times must fall on this grid.

retry_asks.description: How many times the agent asks for another time after an offer that is not allowed, before giving up.

ask_time_template.description: Asks for a clock time when only a day was given.

invalid_template.description: Says the offered day or time is not possible and asks for another one, naming the allowed days and times in words.

on_no_answer.description: Situation when the third party gives no usable answer to when the person can be reached.

terminations.description: Facts about the line or the intended person, learnt before identity is verified, that end the call at once with no further question (each from the brief). Requests and refusals (wanting a human, not wanting to talk, asking to stop) are not terminations: they are events, which this spec version keeps in residual_rules.

trigger.description: What the person says, in the brief's words; it becomes an extraction label.

questions.description: The security questions in the order they are asked.

field.description: The value the verification tool takes to name this question (one of its enum values).

reask_template.description: Asks the same question again after a wrong or unreadable answer.

digits_count.description: For digits: the exact number of digits expected.

api_format.description: The form the tool expects, in words or as a pattern.

complete_pattern.description: Python regular expression that the normalised answer must match in full before the tool is called.

numeric_date_order.description: For a date said only in numbers: the order to read it in.

total_wrong.description: Wrong answers in total that end the check.

per_question_wrong.description: Wrong answers to one question that end the check.

on_wrong.description: After a wrong answer that does not end the check: ask the same question again, or move on.

hints.description: Hints the verification tool can return, and what the agent does with each.

value.description: The hint value exactly as the tool returns it.

question.description: The question field it applies to, or any.

explain_template.description: Said when the person does not want to answer: why the questions are asked.

max_refusals.description: The refusal that closes the call (a second refusal closes = 2).

purpose_question.description: Asking what the call is about instead of answering: counted with refusals, counted on its own counter with the same limit, or not a refusal.

disclosure.description: What the agent says right after identity is verified, before asking for anything.

intro_template.description: Said once: who is calling and why.

kind.description: The product kind value as the lookup tool returns it.

name_template.description: The product in words; may use fields of the product row as {{field}}.

amount.description: Expression for the amount of the first ask, per product.

date.description: Expression for the date of the first ask.

scope.description: With several products: one first ask for all of them, or one per product.

template.description: The first ask, with one product.

template_multi.description: The first ask, with several products.

non_business_day.description: The customer names a day that is not a business day and not after the deadline.

policy.description: Offer the next or the previous business day instead, or ask for another day.

template.description: Offers the shifted day (next or prev): date is the business day offered, named_date the day the customer named.

after_deadline.description: The customer names a day after the product's deadline.

policy.description: Offer the deadline itself, or ask for another day.

template.description: Offers the deadline (offer_deadline): date is the deadline, named_date the day the customer named.

vague.description: The customer gives a period or an event instead of a day (a week, a month, a payday).

re_asks.description: How many times the agent asks for the exact day.

then.description: Still no exact day after the re-asks: propose the deadline, or treat it as a non-answer.

propose_template.description: Proposes the deadline (propose_deadline): date is the deadline.

ask_date_template.description: Asks for another day when the day named cannot be used (it has passed, or the policy is ask). Agent-proposed amounts only: never ask how much the customer can pay.

ladder.description: The persuasion attempts in order. A flat refusal of the offer on the table uses one attempt: the next step that applies to the product's band is offered, until the band's attempts are used up. The engine keeps every offered date a business day from today up to the deadline.

bands.description: Ids of the bands this step applies to; empty = every band.

template.description: The offer, ending with a question.

non_answer_is_refusal.description: true when the material counts a non-answer to an offer like a flat refusal.

dedupe_refused_offers.description: true when an offer the customer already refused must not be made again (a step that would repeat one is skipped).

on_exhausted.description: Situation when the attempts are used up.

multi.description: A customer with several late products.

product_intro_template.description: Said before the first offer for each product when the products are gone through one by one.

overflow.description: One day named for all products that is after one product's deadline: that product takes its own deadline, or the agent asks for another day.

overflow_note_template.description: Added to a read-back line whose product took its own deadline: date is that deadline.

failed_promise.description: A promise that cannot be recorded among several: keep the others (the product gets the failure situation's note), or end the call with the failure situation.

amounts.description: Amounts. The agent proposes every amount; it never asks how much the customer can pay.

accept_range.description: Amounts the customer proposes that are accepted: from the floor up to the full amount due, or only the full amount. A higher amount is read as the full amount.

too_much.description: The customer says the amount is too much.

policy.description: Offer the floor (on the date on the table), or treat it as a flat refusal.

template.description: Offers the floor: amount is the floor, date the date on the table.

below_floor.description: The customer proposes an amount below the floor.

template.description: Says the amount cannot be recorded and offers the floor: named_amount is the customer's amount, amount the floor.

floor_offers.description: How many times too_much and below_floor together may offer the floor (the ladder may name it again).

same_amount_template.description: A ladder offer that keeps the amount just refused and only moves the date, so the amount is not offered again in so many words.

products.description: How each late product from the lookup tool is classified.

bands.description: The bands the material sorts products into (for example by days overdue), in its order; the first band whose selector is true applies. When the material has no bands: one band with selector True.

selector.description: true for a product in this band.

deadline.description: Expression for the latest promise date of a product in this band.

attempts.description: Persuasion attempts for a product in this band.

action.description: negotiate a promise, or end the call with the situation (a transfer when it has a queue).

floor.description: Expression for the lowest amount that can be recorded for a product.

unmatched.description: Situation when no band applies to a product.

failure_policy.description: What the agent does when a bank tool fails (an error status, a timeout, or ok not true).

item_template.description: One agreed promise inside the read-back.

question.description: The confirmation question, exactly as the brief words it.

on_change.description: The customer changes a value at the confirmation step.

recording_template.description: Said before the bank write; claims nothing.

recorded_template.description: Said after the tool confirmed the write.

after_recorded_sentence.description: A sentence the brief requires after a recorded promise.

change_after_record_template.description: Reply when the customer wants to change a recorded promise.

on_recorded.description: Situation once at least one promise is recorded (unless a later situation such as a transfer overrides it).

events.description: Things a customer may say that change the course of the call (a payment already made, a dispute, hardship, a request for a human or a new plan, not wanting to talk), in order of precedence: when one message fits several, the first listed applies.

trigger.description: What the customer says, in the material's words; it becomes an extraction label.

stages.description: Stages in which it applies (negotiate and confirm are after verification).

min_occurrences.description: How many times the customer must say it before it applies (a rule that needs it said twice = 2).

suppresses.description: Ids of events that no longer apply once this one did, and persuasion when no persuasion attempt may follow it (a refusal then ends the call with on_no).

below_min_template.description: Said, as the whole reply, when it was said fewer than min_occurrences times (for example a question whether the agent can help first); not_specified: the message is handled as usual.

template.description: Said when it applies. When it ends with a yes/no question, on_yes and on_no say what follows.

on_no.description: Also used when the customer refuses a payment after this event suppressed persuasion.

then.description: What follows when the template asks no question.

then_before_verification.description: Replaces then (and on_yes) before identity is verified; not_specified = the same.

several_products.description: With several products: the event ends only the product it concerns (it gets the situation's note and the call goes on with the others), or it ends the call.

side_questions.description: Questions a customer asks that the agent answers before it goes on with what it was asking.

trigger.description: The question, in the material's words; it becomes an extraction label.

template.description: The answer; it reveals nothing about the account, so it may be said before verification.

policy.description: answer_from_facts: answered in one sentence from the facts the tools gave (none before verification); no_info: always the no-information sentence.

no_info_template.description: Says the agent does not have that information.

notes.description: Notes the agent writes for products without a recorded promise.

enabled.description: true when every product without a promise gets a note (the reason is the note_reason of the situation that ended it, or of the closing situation).

on_transfer.description: Notes when the call is transferred: none at all (drop), or as usual (keep).

text_template.description: The note's free text, if the tool takes one.

situations.description: Every way a call can end. One entry per (outcome, reason) and per distinct thing to say.

reason.description: The close tool's reason value; empty when the outcome takes none.

queue.description: The transfer queue when this situation hands the call over; empty otherwise.

note_reason.description: The note reason a product gets in this situation when notes are written; empty otherwise.

say.description: Sentences the brief requires right before the farewell; empty when none.

farewell.description: The last words of the call.

reasons.description: Allowed reasons; empty when the outcome takes no reason.

transfer_overrides_promise.description: A transfer after a recorded promise closes as the transfer.

aggregation.description: With several products and no recorded promise: when every product ended in the same situation, that one; otherwise the situation of the first product, in lookup order, whose note reason is not in skip_note_reasons.

hangup.description: The situation used when the line drops in each stage. stated_in_brief false: the brief is silent and you picked the closest situation.

phrases.description: Every sentence the brief prescribes word for word, and where the spec uses it.

used_in.description: Spec paths of the templates that contain it, or residual:<id>.

residual_rules.description: Every rule the sections above cannot express.

text.description: The rule, self-contained, with every value.

class.description: speech: only wording or tone. flow: changes a tool call, an outcome, an amount, a date or a count.

trigger.description: For flow: what in the conversation starts it. Empty for speech.

rule_index.description: Every binding digest rule, once, with the spec paths or residual ids that carry it.

forbidden_codes.description: Code values (outcomes, reasons, queues, note reasons or other enum values) that the material forbids the agent to send, for example codes reserved for back-office staff. Never a tool name: a tool the agent must not call is simply left out of bindings.tools, and the rule is indexed where it is enforced.
